[[Federal Islamic Republic of the Comoros|Comoros]] sent a delegation to compete at the [[2000 Summer Olympics]] in [[Sydney]], Australia from 15 September to 1 October 2000.  This was the Indian Ocean nation's second appearance at a [[Summer Olympic Games]], following their debut four years earlier at the [[1996 Atlanta Olympics]].  The delegation consisted of two [[track and field]] athletes: [[Hadhari Djaffar]] and [[Sandjema Batouli]].  Both raced in the [[100 metres at the Olympics|100 meters]] events, but neither advanced beyond the first round.

==Background==
The Comité Olympique et Sportif des Iles Comores (the [[National Olympic Committee]] (NOC) of the Comoros Islands) was recognized by the [[International Olympic Committee]] on 1 January 1993.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/comoros|title=Comoros – National Olympic Committee (NOC)|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=25 October 2018}}</ref> Comoros joined Olympic competition at the [[1996 Summer Olympics]] and have participated at every [[Summer Olympic Games]] since, though the nation has yet to debut at the [[Winter Olympic Games]].<ref name="COMSR">{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/COM/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417093051/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/COM/|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|title=Comoros|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=25 October 2018}}</ref>  Sydney was the second appearance by the nation in a Summer Olympiad.<ref name="COMSR" />  The 2000 Summer Olympics were held from 15 September to 1 October 2000; a total of 10,651 athletes represented 199 NOCs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/sydney-2000|title=Sydney 2000 Summer Olympics – results & video highlights|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=7 August 2018}}</ref>  The Comoros delegation to Sydney consisted of two [[track and field]] athletes: [[Hadhari Djaffar]] and [[Sandjema Batouli]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/COM/summer/2000/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417093050/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/COM/summer/2000/|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|title=Comoros at the 2000 Sydney Summer Games|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=25 October 2018}}</ref>

== Athletics ==
{{main|Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics}}

Sandjema Batouli was 18 years old at the time of the Sydney Olympics and was making her only Olympic appearance.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ba/sandjema-batouli-1.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200418074417/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ba/sandjema-batouli-1.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 April 2020|title=Sandjema Batouli Bio, Stats, and Results|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=25 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/sandjema-batouli|title=Sandjema BATOULI – Olympic Athletics – Comoros|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=25 October 2018}}</ref>  On 23 September, she participated in the first round of the [[Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metres|women's 100 metres]] and was drawn into heat nine.  She finished the race in a time of 13.58 seconds, ninth and last in her heat, and was not able to progress to the next round.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/2000/ATH/womens-100-metres-round-one.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417051941/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/2000/ATH/womens-100-metres-round-one.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|title=Athletics at the 2000 Sydney Summer Games: Women's 100 metres Round One|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=25 October 2018}}</ref> In the event overall, the gold medal is vacant due to original gold medalist [[Marion Jones]] of the [[United States at the 2000 Summer Olympics|United States]] admitting to steroid use and forfeiting her medals and results from the Sydney Games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/olympics/trackandfield/news/story?id=3054706|title=Jones returns five medals from 2000 Sydney Olympics|date=8 October 2007|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=7 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180801064333/http://www.espn.com/olympics/trackandfield/news/story?id=3054706|archive-date=1 August 2018|url-status=live|df=dmy-all| agency = [[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref name=Guardian>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2009/dec/07/marion-jones-2000-olympic-medals|title=Marion Jones's medals from Sydney Olympics to be reallocated|date=7 December 2009|publisher=[[TheGuardian.com]]| agency = [[Associated Press]]|access-date=7 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160622022018/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2009/dec/07/marion-jones-2000-olympic-medals|archive-date=22 June 2016|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  Officially, the medals in the event are held by [[Ekaterini Thanou]] of [[Greece at the 2000 Summer Olympics|Greece]] and [[Tayna Lawrence]] (the original bronze medalist) of [[Jamaica at the 2000 Summer Olympics|Jamaica]] sharing silver, and [[Merlene Ottey]], also of Jamaica, the original fourth-place finisher, being awarded a bronze.<ref name="Guardian" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/sydney-2000/athletics/100m-women|title=Sydney 2000 100m women – Olympic Athletics|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=24 October 2018}}</ref>  Gold was left vacant because Thanou, the original silver medalist, had her own issue with missing a drug test at the [[2004 Summer Olympics]]<ref name="Guardian" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/09/07/sports/olympics/peculiar-greek-doping-case-takes-another-twist.html|title=Peculiar Greek Doping Case Takes Another Twist|last=Macur|first=Juliet|date=6 September 2011|work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=10 August 2018}}</ref>

Hadhari Djaffar was 21 years old at the time of these Games.  He was already a veteran of the 1996 Summer Olympics, and would later go on to represent the [[Comoros at the 2004 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/dj/hadhari-djaffar-1.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200418005814/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/dj/hadhari-djaffar-1.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 April 2020|title=Hadhari Djaffar Bio, Stats, and Results|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=25 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/hadhari-djaffar|title=Hadhari DJAFFAR – Olympic Athletics – Comoros|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=25 October 2018}}</ref>  On 22 September, he participated in the first round heats of the [[Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's 100 metres|men's 100 metres]] and was drawn into heat seven.  He completed the race in a time of 10.68 seconds, seventh out of nine competitors in his heat.<ref name="M100mR1" /> His time was insufficient to advance, as 10.48 seconds was the slowest qualifying time.<ref name="M100mR1">{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/2000/ATH/mens-100-metres-round-one.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417094018/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/2000/ATH/mens-100-metres-round-one.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|title=Athletics at the 2000 Sydney Summer Games: Men's 100 metres Round One|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=25 October 2018}}</ref> The gold medal was eventually won in 9.87 seconds by [[Maurice Greene (athlete)|Maurice Greene]] of the United States, the silver was won by [[Ato Boldon]] of [[Trinidad and Tobago at the 2000 Summer Olympics|Trinidad and Tobago]], and the bronze was earned by [[Obadele Thompson]] of [[Barbados at the 2000 Summer Olympics|Barbados]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/2000/ATH/mens-100-metres.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417094402/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/2000/ATH/mens-100-metres.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|title=Athletics at the 2000 Sydney Summer Games: Men's 100 metres|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=24 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/sydney-2000/athletics/100m-men|title=Sydney 2000 100m men – Olympic Athletics|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=24 October 2018}}</ref>
